scenes.heading: Angles of elevation and depression
scenes.sub: Measure a building without climbing it
scenes.say: How tall is that building? How far away is that boat? You can find out without a tape measure. Just measure the angle you look up or down, and use trigonometry.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Tilt your head up to see a bird, down to see your shoes
scenes.science: Up from horizontal = elevation; down = depression
scenes.breaks: Your eyes are above the ground, so sometimes you must add your eye height to the answer.
scenes.say: Look straight ahead: that's the horizontal. Tilt your head up to see a bird: that's an angle of elevation. Tilt it down to see your shoes: that's an angle of depression. Both start from the horizontal.

scenes.heading: Angle of elevation
notes: Turn UP to the line of sight
scenes.say: First the dashed horizontal line from your eye. Then the line of sight up to the bird. The angle between them, theta, is the angle of elevation.

scenes.heading: Depression = elevation
notes: Horizontal at the top ∥ the ground
scenes.say: Here's a cliff and a boat. Looking down from the cliff top, the angle of depression is thirty degrees, measured from the horizontal. The horizontal is parallel to the ground, so by alternate angles, the angle of elevation from the boat is also thirty degrees.
scenes.caption: Angle of depression from the top = angle of elevation from the bottom (alternate angles).

scenes.heading: Height of a tree
scenes.question: You are 30 m from a tree. The angle of elevation to the top is 38°. Find its height.
scenes.say: You stand thirty metres from a tree and look up at thirty-eight degrees. The height is opposite and the thirty metres is adjacent, so use tan. h equals thirty times tan thirty-eight, about twenty-three point four metres.
scenes.caption: tan 38° = h/30, so h = 30 × tan 38° ≈ 23.4 m.

scenes.heading: Boat from a cliff
scenes.question: An 80 m cliff. Angle of depression to a boat: 24°. How far is the boat from the base?
scenes.say: From an eighty metre cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is twenty-four degrees. By alternate angles, that's also the angle at the boat. Tan twenty-four equals eighty over x, so x equals eighty divided by tan twenty-four, about one hundred and seventy-nine point seven metres.
scenes.caption: tan 24° = 80/x, so x = 80 ÷ tan 24° ≈ 179.7 m.

scenes.heading: Don’t forget eye height
scenes.say: Your eyes are one point six metres above the ground. From eye level, twenty-five times tan fifty-two is about thirty-two metres. That's only the part above your eyes, so add one point six. The building is about thirty-three point six metres tall.
scenes.caption: 25 × tan 52° ≈ 32.0 m, plus 1.6 m eye height ≈ 33.6 m.

points: Both angles start at the horizontal
Sketch the triangle; SOH CAH TOA
scenes.say: Recap. Both angles are measured from the horizontal: elevation looks up, depression looks down, and they are equal alternate angles. Sketch the right-angled triangle, use SOH CAH TOA, and add eye height when it's given. Now try the practice questions!
